title: Florida House, District 27
what_it_does: Represents District 27 in the Florida House of Representatives; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: On the Nov. 3 ballot. The Florida Division of Elections 2026 general-election candidate list (checked Oct. 7, 2026) shows 2 qualified candidates: Andy Ferrari (Democrat), Richard Gentry (Republican). An earlier version of this guide marked the seat as decided, based on a report published before candidate qualifying closed on June 12; that was wrong. Source: https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp

candidates.name: Richard Gentry
candidates.occupation: Attorney; former staff of the state Office of Public Counsel
candidates.background: Richard Gentry, a Volusia County native who lives in Astor, is an attorney with law and undergraduate degrees from the University of Miami. His campaign says he most recently advocated for consumers before the Public Service Commission and earlier worked with builders and communities on the Growth Management Act and the Sadowski affordable-housing act. He was elected to the House in 2024.

taxes.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

property_tax.summary: Voted for CS/HJR 1-F (2026), the June 2026 joint resolution that placed Amendment 3 on the ballot to raise the non-school homestead exemption to $250,000 by 2028 and let counties and cities exempt homesteads entirely; because the vote sent the question to voters rather than cutting taxes itself, a vote for it is coded as leaning toward sharply reducing homestead property taxes rather than as full agreement.

His platform also lists putting election security and integrity at the forefront of policy.

candidates.name: Andy Ferrari
candidates.occupation: Administrative assistant at an accounting firm; notary public; owner of A+ Rides
candidates.background: Andy Ferrari, 49, lives in DeLeon Springs in Volusia County and holds an associate degree in psychology from Daytona State College. He was the Democratic nominee for House District 27 in 2024, losing to Republican Richard Gentry with about 30% of the vote, and is challenging Gentry again in 2026. In his 2026 VOTE411 answers he names housing prices, property insurance and public schools as his top concerns.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

abortion.summary: In his 2026 League of Women Voters questionnaire he said he supports full access to abortion.
abortion.quote: I support any and all access to Abortion. I believe that Abortion should be legal, free and rare.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 27 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

housing.summary: He said he would support a bill capping how much residential housing costs can rise by law, along with tax incentives for small landlords who own up to five rental houses.
housing.quote: I would support any bill that caps the amount of increase allowed by law on residential housing.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 27 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

property_tax.summary: Asked about property insurance and taxes, he warned that if Amendment 3 (the 2026 homestead-exemption increase) passes, Volusia County special-district taxes could be replaced by fees without limits.
property_tax.quote: If Amendment 3 passes, all those current taxes (limited by law) could become fees with no maximum limit.

sources.title: VOTE411 (League of Women Voters) 2026 general election guide, State Representative 27 (candidate's own answers; accessed Oct. 7, 2026)
